strings.name: Daniela Rus
strings.summary: Born in Romania, Rus moved to the United States, studied computing and mathematics and completed doctoral training at Cornell. She established robotics research at Dartmouth, later joined MIT and became CSAIL director in 2012. Her work spans distributed, self-reconfiguring and soft robots, autonomous systems and human collaboration, integrating bodies, algorithms and environments. She also writes about robotics and AI in society; the research depends on interdisciplinary teams.

strings.influence.rationale: Advanced research in robotics, distributed systems and intelligent manufacturing, exploring technical approaches to autonomous machines and collaboration with people.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: University of Iowa bachelor’s in computing and mathematics (1985); Cornell computer science doctorate (1992, following MIT and MacArthur sources).
strings.highlights.h1.title: Reconfigurable and soft robots
strings.highlights.h1.text: Studies self-reconfiguring systems, soft bodies and control methods that help robots adapt to environments.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Distributed intelligence and collaboration
strings.highlights.h2.text: Combines algorithms, sensing and physical structure to investigate autonomous machines and human interaction.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Publishing robotics and AI books
strings.timeline.t1.text: Coauthored The Heart and the Chip and The Mind’s Mirror, discussing technology’s applications for the public.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Reviewing soft robotics
strings.timeline.t2.text: Published a Nature review on design, fabrication and control with Michael Tolley.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Becoming CSAIL director
strings.timeline.t3.text: Became director of MIT’s Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Joining MIT
strings.timeline.t4.text: Moved from Dartmouth to continue robotics and computing research at MIT.
strings.timeline.t5.title: MacArthur Fellowship
strings.timeline.t5.text: Received recognition for integrating self-reconfiguring robots and computing theory.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Founding Dartmouth’s robotics laboratory
strings.timeline.t6.text: Built a university team applying distributed algorithms to working robotic systems.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Completing Cornell doctoral training
strings.timeline.t7.text: Earned a computer science doctorate, then pursued robotics and distributed systems.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Earning an Iowa degree
strings.timeline.t8.text: Completed undergraduate computing and mathematics before graduate study.
